This scientist is sliding a live pigeon into the nose of a bomb. And no, he's not getting rid of it. He actually wants the pigeon to fly it!

It's World War Two, and bombs keep missing their targets. So a psychologist named B.F. Skinner shows up with a plan, and a box full of pigeons. The officials think it's a joke, but they give him twenty-five thousand dollars anyway.

Here's the trick. A lens in the nose shows the target on a little screen, and the pigeon pecks right at it. If the bomb drifts, the picture slides, the pigeon chases it, and every peck steers it back. One single pigeon pecked ten thousand times in forty-five minutes!
But what if a pigeon gets confused? Easy. Just put in three! You see, it's like asking three friends for directions. If two of them point the same way, you go that way.

The officials were amused, not impressed, and in 1944 it was cancelled. But after the war, the Navy brought the pigeons back! And it kept running until 1953, when electronics finally got as good as a pigeon.
